title: What is a budget
text: A budget is a plan for how much money you expect to spend in different categories over a period, usually a month. In this app, the Budget Manager module lets a user set a target amount for a month and compare it against actual spending recorded in the Expense & Category Manager.

title: What is an expense category
text: An expense category groups similar spending together, such as Groceries, Transport, or Entertainment. The Expense & Category Manager module lets each user create their own categories and assign every expense to one category so spending can be tracked by category.

title: Budget Manager module overview
text: The Budget Manager module lets a user create a monthly budget with per-category limits, list existing budgets, and update or delete them. It is the Student 1 feature and stores its data in its own SQLite database, separate from the other four modules.

title: Expense & Category Manager module overview
text: The Expense & Category Manager module lets a user record individual expenses, assign them to a category, and view their expense history filtered by category. It is the Student 2 feature and includes an AI assistant that can suggest a category for a new expense.

title: Income & Pay Schedule Manager module overview
text: The Income & Pay Schedule Manager module tracks a user's income sources (such as a salary or freelance income) and the pay schedule for each one, including payment frequency and standard amount. It is the Student 3 feature.

title: Bill Manager module overview
text: The Bill Manager module tracks recurring and one-off bills, their due dates, and their status (Pending, Paid, or Overdue). It also provides a summary of total and pending bill amounts. It is the Student 4 feature.

title: Savings Goal Manager module overview
text: The Savings Goal Manager module lets a user set a savings goal with a target amount and track progress toward it over time. It is the Student 5 feature.

title: How to add an expense
text: To add an expense in the Expense & Category Manager, choose or create a category, enter the amount and a short description, and set the date. The expense is then stored against the logged-in user's account and appears in their expense history.

title: How to create a budget
text: To create a budget in the Budget Manager, choose the month and year, then set a target spending amount for one or more categories. The app compares this target against the total of the user's recorded expenses in the same categories.

title: What happens when you exceed your budget
text: If a user's recorded expenses in a category exceed the budgeted amount for that month, the Budget Manager flags the category as over budget. The current implementation does not block further spending; it is informational rather than restrictive.

title: How savings goal progress is tracked
text: A savings goal has a target amount and a current saved amount. Progress is shown as the percentage of the target amount that has been saved so far, letting a user see at a glance how close they are to reaching their goal.

title: What a pay schedule is
text: A pay schedule describes how often and how much a particular income source pays, for example a fortnightly salary or a monthly freelance invoice. Each income source in the Income & Pay Schedule Manager can have its own pay schedule.

title: What bill statuses mean
text: A bill in the Bill Manager can be Pending (not yet due or not yet paid), Paid (settled), or Overdue (past its due date and still unpaid). The bill summary endpoint reports the total amount, the pending amount, and the count of overdue bills.

title: What the AI assistant (AI-Mode) does
text: AI-Mode is a shared assistant feature used across all five modules. It runs a small, locally hosted open-source language model (such as Qwen 2.5) and can answer questions about a user's own data or, in some modules, suggest a category or explain a figure using an agentic tool-calling loop.

title: General tips for saving money
text: Common budgeting advice includes tracking every expense so spending patterns become visible, setting a realistic monthly budget per category rather than one lump sum, and automatically directing a fixed amount toward a savings goal before spending the rest.

title: Tips for reducing overspending
text: To reduce overspending, review categories that are frequently over budget, look for recurring but avoidable expenses, and check the Bill Manager for overdue bills, since late fees on overdue bills can make overspending worse.

title: Fixed vs variable expenses
text: A fixed expense stays roughly the same each period, such as rent or a subscription, while a variable expense changes month to month, such as groceries or entertainment. Bills tracked in the Bill Manager are usually fixed expenses; day-to-day spending in the Expense & Category Manager is often variable.

title: How the app separates data between users
text: Most modules scope their data by a user_id, so one user's expenses, categories, bills, income sources, or budgets are not shown to another user. The Savings Goal module is a known exception: its current implementation does not filter goals by user.

title: Common budgeting mistakes
text: Common mistakes include setting a budget once and never checking it again, ignoring small recurring expenses that add up over time, and not tracking irregular income sources like freelance work, which the Income & Pay Schedule Manager is designed to help with.

title: How AI-assisted expense categorisation works
text: When enabled, the Expense & Category Manager's assistant can look at an expense's description and amount and suggest which existing category it most likely belongs to, using the shared AI-Mode language model rather than a fixed set of keyword rules.

title: Why overdue bills matter
text: An overdue bill is one that has passed its due date without being marked paid. Beyond the immediate cost, overdue bills often carry late fees or interest charges from the biller, and repeated overdue bills can affect a person's credit record outside of this app.

title: Categories vs savings goals
text: An expense category (used in the Expense & Category Manager) groups spending you have already made. A savings goal (used in the Savings Goal Manager) is forward-looking: it tracks money being set aside for a future target, rather than money already spent.

title: Tracking multiple income sources
text: A user can add more than one income source in the Income & Pay Schedule Manager, for example a main job and a side gig, each with its own payment frequency and standard amount, so total expected income can be seen across all sources.

title: Why this assistant only answers from retrieved context
text: To avoid making up information, the RAG-backed assistant only answers using the knowledge chunks retrieved for a given question. If no chunk is a good enough match for the question, it reports that it does not have enough information rather than guessing.
